In this paper, a pricing method based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed to maximize the cumulative gain of the load aggregator. The responsive behavior of demand resources is affected by the price generated by the load aggregator which dynamically adjusts its compensation price in an optimal way to maximize its return in a longer time horizon. Experimental simulation is conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed pricing model.

articleTitle: A Deep Convolutional Neural Network Technique for Power Losses Estimation in Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Estimating and analyzing the abrupt changes in the power grid is a difficult task. These changes are nonlinear, uncertain and of higher orders which lead to certain losses in power grid. Stability and reliability of power grid network is affected by excessive power losses. A fast, accurate and stable algorithm is needed to estimate the actual condition of power grid in order to minimize the losses. This paper proposed a real-time technique which estimates the actual power losses in distribution system. Deep convolutional neural network power loss estimation (DCNN-PLE) method is proposed for calculating distribution network losses on the cost of less computation and complexity. The proposed method achieves high accuracy and less execution time as compared to other traditional methods. Root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) are used as evaluation metrics. The experimental and simulation results show that the proposed method achieves better accuracy for 69bus distribution system in estimating the network losses.

articleTitle: Decentralized Distributionally Robust Coordinated Dispatch of Multi-area Power Systems Considering Voltage Security
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a new dispatch approach for multiarea power systems is proposed, where active power and reactive power are simultaneously optimized in a decentralized manner with the aid of reactive power support from conventional generators and wind farms. The automatic voltage control (AVC) strategy for conventional generators and wind farms is employed to mitigate the risk of under-or over-voltage and thus the voltage security will be ensured in the optimization. According to the proposed approach, the admissible regions of wind power is also optimized via striking a balance between the operational cost and risk. On the other hand, considering that in practice, it is hard to exactly estimate the true probability distribution of wind power, the distributionally robust optimization is utilized in the proposed approach to account for the uncertainty of wind power probability distributions. In addition, to improve the computational efficiency, an efficient algorithm is also developed. Numerical results illustrate that compared with the conventional decentralized dispatch approaches, the proposed decentralized approach can obtain more optimal dispatch decisions in terms of operational costs and renewable utilization.

articleTitle: Multi-time Load Restoration Model in Unbalanced Electrical Distribution System Based on Rolling Optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Natural disasters or man-made attacks highlight the urgency of improving resilience of unbalanced distribution networks. Therefore, automatic and fast restoration operations are required to restoring the affected systems. This paper proposes a multi-time load restoration model in unbalanced electrical distribution system. Moreover, considering that this proposed optimization model containing a large number of time-coupled variables and constraints, which will increase the complexity of the optimization problem, we employ the rolling optimization method to reduce the solution complexity and periodically update the restoration schedules. The applicability of the proposed multi-time model and the effectiveness of the proposed approximation and optimization methods are validated on modified IEEE 13-bus and IEEE 37-bus test systems.

articleTitle: Neutral Current Characteristics and Suppression Strategies of Transformers in Urban Substations
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In urban substations near the rail transit, abnormal cases appear frequently in the grounding transformers, which can cause negative effects in the operation of the power system. This phenomenon attracts the attention of the researchers, and ultimately points to the invading stray current leaked from the rail transit nearby. Based on the measurement results in the substation, the characteristics of the neutral current in the grounding transformer are analyzed. In this way, the relationship between the change of transformer neutral current and the operation of rail transit is presented. Then the cause of harmonics in the current is modeled and analyzed. At last, a new suppression strategy for the current is proposed. For verification, the simulation proves the effectiveness of the whole research.

articleTitle: Maintenance Optimization for Combined Heat and Power Unit Based on Opportunistic Maintenance Strategy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Integrated energy system is composed of different multiple energy systems. When the combined heat and power (CHP) unit fails, more than one energy systems can be influenced. Therefore, it is very important to improve the reliability of CHP unit. In this paper, we propose a maintenance decision making model for CHP unit based on opportunistic maintenance strategy. Firstly, the expression of the availability of CHP unit considering opportunistic maintenance is derived. And then, in order to quantify the impact of different maintenance strategies on system operation, system operation risk is given taking electrical load loss and thermal load loss into account. Finally, maintenance decision making model of the CHP unit is established with maintenance constraints. Case studies show that the model can optimize maintenance strategies and improve the reliability of CHP unit and the overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Hybrid Model for Forecasting Locational Marginal Prices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: It has generally become a challenging task to accurately forecast locational marginal prices (LMPs) due to its strong volatility originated from transmission congestion and extreme weather. Most of existing literature fails to predict both price spikes and normal prices with equally satisfying effectiveness. In fact, normal price prediction mostly relies on the strong correlation with demand, which proves to have a high Pearson correlation coefficient with load changes. However, price spikes prediction is associated with network congestion resulting from features with high Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC). In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based hybrid model for LMPs prediction, considering the discrepancy of two kinds of price. Based on a support vector machine (SVM) and a given threshold, we firstly distinguish and label normal prices and price spikes. For normal prices, a long-short term memory (LSTM) neural network can uncover the trend of time series and bring out an accurate prediction. For price spikes, a light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) is adopted to address those extreme jumps by analyzing relevant features in tabular format. Case studies based on realistic datasets from the PJM market demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed hybrid model.

articleTitle: Parallel Operation Analysis and Optimization of Cables in Urban DC Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the rapid development of national energy conservation and emission reduction policies, the wide connection to the distribution network with photovoltaic, energy storage and electric vehicles, and the increasing number of power electronic equipment made the DC distribution system an important development direction. In the future DC distribution system, as the line load continues to increase, more and more single-core cables work in parallel with multiple cables of the same pole., and how to evenly distribute the parallel circuit current has always been a key issue restricting the parallel operation of the cable in same-pole. Starting from the operation control of grid connected AC/DC converter under unbalanced grid voltage, this paper gives theoretical derivation that the busbar current of DC system always has double frequency harmonics. Then, referring to the three-phase AC system, based on the impedance parameter calculation method of“conductor-earth”, the calculation method of AC impedance parameters of multi-circuit cable lines in symmetrical bipolar and monopole DC system is deduced. On the basis of the theoretical analysis, conclusion is put forward, which is, in symmetrical monopole DC system, the current sharing is the best when the mutual impedance between the positive and negative pole cables is equal in each circuit. Finally, supported by a symmetrical bipolar DC power distribution demonstration project in Shenzhen, this paper optimizes the DC bus layout scheme with two cables running in parallel through the finite element calculation. It also verifies derivation of harmonic current sharing in the symmetrical monopole DC system proposed in this paper.

Author Keywords: Parallel operation of the same polarity cables

articleTitle: Optimal Bidding Strategy for Data Center Aggregators Considering Spatio-Temporal Transfer Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: To reduce the cost of load aggregators (LA), recent studies suggest optimizing LA's bidding plans by utilizing the demand response (DR) potential of various flexible end consumers. With the exploding growth of IT demand, an emerging flexible end consumer, data centers, has begun to appear around the world. In this paper, we focus on utilizing the data centers' DR potential to optimize the bidding plans of data center aggregators (DCA), which is the LA that supply power for multiple data centers. First, an optimization bidding model is formulated based on data centers' DR potential, which consider the backup energy characteristics and workloads spatiotemporal transfer characteristics of data centers. Then, in view of the unique load characteristics of data centers, we propose a rational and quantitative compensation mechanism for the DCA to induce data centers participating in DR. In the end, simulation results are used to prove that the proposed model is beneficial to both the DCA and data centers.

articleTitle: Research on Single-Stage Five-Level Grid-Connected Inverter for Wide Input Voltage Range
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Photovoltaic cells are affected by factors, such as external radiation and temperature, their output voltages have wide range. For adopting to the wide input voltage range from photovoltaic, a novel single-stage five-level grid-connected inverter is proposed in the paper, and the functions of inverter and boost are realized in the transformation. Compared with the traditional multi-level grid-connected inverter, the inverter has the advantages of buck-boost, simple topology, easy control, fewer power devices, and lower switching losses. First, the topology of the inverter is designed and the feasibility and working mode is analyzed. Then, on the basis of the analysis of current sharing characteristics, the inverter's operating mode is analyzed. Based on the traditional PR control method, the model predictive control algorithm is used to control the inverter on the grid. Moreover, the control principles and control process of the modulation method are introduced. At last, the proposed grid-connected inverter is closed-loop designed and simulated, and the feasibility of the topology is verified.

articleTitle: Distributed Robust Dynamic Economic Dispatch of Integrated Transmission and Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: To coordinate the generation resources located in the integrated transmission and distribution systems (ITD) considering renewable uncertainty, dynamic economic dispatch (DED) is essential. In this paper, a coordinated robust DED (CRDED) model is proposed to enhance the cost-effectiveness and reliability in a system perspective. A distributed framework based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is presented to solve this model in a decentralized way, with the transmission and distribution systems solve their regional problems autonomously. To handle the problem that it is hard to predetermine the value of penalty factors, a varying penalty factor strategy is further applied to enhance the convergence property of ADMM, with the global optimal solution achieved within much fewer iteration numbers. Since only the boundary power needs to be exchanged between the transmission and distribution systems, the communication burden is light and the regional information of different operators is encrypted. Case studies on the T118D10 system illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and approach.

Author Keywords: integrated transmission and distribution systemb robust optimization

articleTitle: Optimal Daily Storage Operation for Industrial and Commercial Load Management
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Industrial and commercial electricity bills, generally include energy charge and demand charge, are significant expenses for the business. Equipping energy storage is a desirable option for user-side load management. This paper formulates a decomposition scheme for the maximum demand in a billing period so that the monthly demand charge can be integrated into the daily cost expression, together with the energy charge. Based on this, an optimal battery scheduling strategy under uncertainty is proposed to minimize the expected electricity costs. Further analysis deduces the convexity of the proposed model, which ensures global optimal solutions. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is demonstrated by a comparison of examples. Also, the impact of the initialP state of charge on cost reduction is evaluated.

articleTitle: Economic Benefit Assessment of Multi-type Flexible Demand Side Resources Paticipating in Valley-filling Market
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Valley-filling markets were established for several provinces in China to accommodate high-level of renewable penetration. Demand side resource is potentially a type of more effective and efficient participant to the market. The paper presents a method to assess economic benefit of multi-type flexible demand side resource participating in valley-filling market. A generic demand side resource model considering power, energy and time-of-use is proposed to schedule the operations of different types of demand side resources. A chronological production cost simulation model considering demand side resource is presented to optimize the actual operation of demand side resources, thermal generators and renewable generation. In order to quantify the economic benefit of demand side resource, a set of indices reflecting benefits of renewable generation and valley-filling market is established. A case study base on an actual power system in North China is performed using the proposed methods. Numerical results show that demand side resource brings great economic benefit to renewable generation and valley-filling market.

articleTitle: An Improved Artificial Neural Network Method for Predicting PV Output Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In order to ensure the safety and stability of the power grid with photovoltaic (PV) generation integration, it is necessary to predict the output performance of PV module under varying operating condition. In this paper, an improved artificial neural network (ANN) method is proposed to predict electrical characteristics of PV module by combining several neural networks under different environmental conditions. In order to study the dependence of output performance on solar irradiance and temperature, the proposed neural networks model is composed of four neural network. Each neural network consists of three layers, in which input is solar radiation and module temperature and output are five physical parameters of single diode model. The experimental data is divided into four groups and used for training the neural networks. The electrical property of PV modules, including I-V curves, P-V curves and normal root mean square error, are obtained and discussed. The effectiveness and accuracy of this method is verified by the experimental data for different type photovoltaic modules. Comparing with traditional single ANN method, the proposed method shows better accuracy under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Economic Dispatch Considering Transmission-Distribution Coordination and Automatic Regulation effect of Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the increase of proportion of renewable energy, the uncertainty in power system is significantly increased, and the security operation of power system is facing more challenges. In traditional economic dispatch model, the unit output and load are expressed by constant power, which ignores the automatic regulation effect during system operation. And the transmission system and distribution system are separated optimized, the coordination effect is not considered. In this paper, a new dynamic economic dispatch model is proposed and the automatic regulation effect and transmission-distribution coordination are considered, which can improve the renewable energy accommodation and enhance the system operation security and economics. The validity and effectiveness of the proposed model are illustrated by case studies.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of PSSs and PODs by Sequential Quadratic Programming with Gradient Sampling
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Due to the nonsmooth property of the spectral abscissa function, the simultaneous coordination of power system stabilizers (PSSs) and power oscillation dampers (PODs) is a nonsmooth constrained optimization problem. How to solve this problem and ensure optimality with convergence guarantees is still an open question. To tackle this computational challenge, this paper proposes a Sequential Quadratic Programming method with Gradient Sampling (SQP-GS) to coordinate and optimize the parameters of PSSs and PODs based on Gradient Sampling theory. At a given iterate, the gradient of the objective function is evaluated on a set of randomly generated nearby points by computing closed-form eigenvalue sensitivities. The method can guarantee that the solution of the optimization problem globally and efficiently converges to stationary points with probability one. Tests on the WSCC 3-machine 9-bus system and New England 10-machine 39-bus system show that the optimality of SQP-GS solution is better than that of heuristic algorithms and conventional tuning method, and the efficiency of the proposed method is comparable with the heuristic algorithms.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Method for Non-intrusive Load Monitoring with Balanced Redundancy and Relevancy
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring(NILM) has become a key technology in the power Internet of Things and an important information source of load characteristics analysis. Whether the selected features are appropriate determines the effectiveness of load identification in NILM. In order to reduce redundance and improve relevance of the selected features, a feature selection method which integrates mutual information and Relief-F algorithm is proposed. Based on the analysis of the power consumption characteristics of various electrical appliances, the prospective components of the initial feature set for NILM is discussed. From the perspective of balancing redundancy and relevancy, the redundant features are removed by using mutual information algorithm, the relevance of the features are sorted by using Relief-F algorithm, and then the optimal feature subset is obtained. A k-NN identification algorithm is applied to test the effectiveness of the feature selection methods. The simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to other filter feature selection methods in robustness and universality, and can significantly improve the identification accuracy.

articleTitle: Residual Power Supply Capacity Evaluation of Distribution Network Considering Dynamic Safety Margin of Second-use Electric Vehicle Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Residual power supply capacity (RSC) is an important indicator for evaluating the distribution network, and as more and more energy storage systems are connected to the distribution network, it is necessary to study the impact of energy storage installation location and its own capacity characteristics on the power supply capacity of the distribution network. This paper considers using second-use energy storage (SUESS) instead of a brand new energy storage system. Firstly, this paper calculates the upper and lower limits of initial capacity of SUESS by calculating the number of retired batteries cycles and establishes the capacity attenuation model of energy storage power plant to determine the capacity attenuation during operation, dynamically updating the safety margin of energy storage. Secondly, the distribution network can be operated in an island after a failure, so this paper proposes a N-l security verification method for the distribution network with SUESS. Finally, this paper integrates the SUESS island operation model to establish the residual power supply capacity (SURSC) model with SUESS. Through analysis and comparison of distribution network examples, this method has advantages in feasibility and can effectively evaluate the remaining power supply capacity of distribution networks with SUESS.

articleTitle: Subsynchronous Oscillation Monitoring and Alarm Method Based on Phasor Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the large-scale grid connection of new energy, a large number of power electronic devices installed introduce sub-/super-synchronous inter-harmonics into power signals, resulting in frequent occurrence of subsynchronous oscillations (SSO). The subsynchronous oscillation will cause serious harm to generator sets and power systems, so its online monitoring and accurate alarm are crucial to the safe and stable operation of them. Phasor measurement units (PMUs) can realize dynamic real-time monitoring of power systems. Based on PMU phasor measurements, this paper proposes a method for SSO online monitoring and alarm on the main station of PMU. Firstly, based on PMU current phasor amplitude data, FFT frequency spectrum analysis is performed to obtain subsynchronous frequency components. Secondly, the SVM learner is trained to obtain the amplitude threshold, then filter out safe components and retain harmful ones. Finally, the adaptive duration threshold is determined according to frequency susceptibility, amplitude attenuation and energy accumulation to decide whether to send out an alarm signal. Experiments based on field data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint Generation, Transmission and Energy Storage Systems Expansion Planning in Multi-area Power Systems Considering Detailed Modeling of Tie lines
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The interconnection of sub-regions through tie lines can improve the overall economy of the system and provide a broad space for renewable energy consumption, such as wind power. However, at present, no detailed models exist for tie lines in the planning of multi-area power systems. In this paper, a novel multi-area and multi-objective model for the generation, transmission, and battery energy storage systems expansion planning is proposed in a central planning method that considers uncertainties of wind power and load. Tie lines among different subareas are used as support power sources, and detailed tie-line expansion planning models that consider the power flow direction, degree of power flow fluctuation, and number of power flow direction reversal in the tie line are presented to make the model more realistic. Besides, short-term operation problems (i.e., unit commitment) are incorporated in the long term planning issues to improve the adaptability of planning schemes. Linearized procedure for the different tie-line operation modes is implemented in order to improve the efficiency of the presented model. The proposed model is finally transformed into a mixedinteger linear programming formulation. The modified IEEE RTS-24 bus system is conducted to evaluate the practicality and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Non-intrusive Load Identification Method Suitable for Home Scene
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Home Energy Management System (HEMS) is strict on the hardware cost of algorithm implementation. In view of the deep learning-based load recognition method, the training process needs to be implemented on high-performance computing equipment, which leads to the problem of increased cost of HEMS hardware. This paper proposes a load identification method based on weighted k-NearestNeighbor (kNN) without training process. First, assign weight to the trajectory feature of each training sample to improve kNN’s recognition accuracy of minority classes. Then, consider the amplitude features of the equipment, and predict the category to which the sample belongs according to the comprehensive similarity based on these two characteristics. Finally, the PLAID dataset is used to verify the algorithm.

articleTitle: Consensus-based Nodal Pricing Mechanism for Automated Demand Response Considering Congestion Management on Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This paper investigates a consensus-based nodal pricing mechanism for incenting automated demand response in the deregulated market environment. These small-scale customers are autonomously managed by automated demand response (DR) controllers, which are capable of scheduling user's load devices to follow a day-ahead 24h price signal from electricity distribution companies (EDC). First, an alternating current optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the distribution network is formulated considering the participation of automated DR. Then, a consensusbased approach is exploited to adjust the nodal price and DR profile for each customer using primal-dual decomposition. The proposed mechanism is compared with a day-ahead pricing (DAP) program on a test distribution network and numerical results have shown promising performance in supporting the congestion management on the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Multi-energy Complementarity Evaluation and Its Interaction with Wind and Photovoltaic Capacity optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: High penetration of renewable energy generation is an important trend in the development of power systems. However, the problem of wind and solar energy curtailment due to their inherent randomness and fluctuation remains to be solved. Multienergy complementary operation based on the complementarity between different renewable energy units is an important means to improve the consumption. In this paper, a complementarity evaluation index is proposed to describe the matching ability of the total output of renewable power generation to the load. The interaction between the proposed index and an optimal allocation model of wind and photovoltaic capacity is analyzed in detail. Based on the analysis of the interaction, we can get a satisfying allocation result simply but effectively by maximizing the index. Compared with the existing complementarity indices, the proposed index can describe the complementarity between renewable energy sources in different capacity allocation results.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Location Based on Improved Romp Algorithm for Compressed Sensing in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The structure of distribution network is complex and has many branches. At the same time, with the increasing proportion of distributed power in the distribution network, the traditional fault location method has been difficult to take into account the cost and accuracy of the method. In this paper, a fault location algorithm based on sparse measurement points is proposed. From the perspective of negative sequence injection current, the mapping relationship between compression sensing theory and distribution network fault location problem is established. The negative sequence node voltage after fault is calculated by fuzzy power flow calculation method, and the base matrix is constructed. The limited isometric property of the sensing matrix is analyzed, and an improved ROMP algorithm is proposed to reconstruct the current signal. A distribution system with multiple distributed power sources is built and simulated in the ieee-33 node distribution system. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional method, the algorithm proposed in this paper has stronger ability to withstand transition resistance and noise, higher accuracy of fault location and better real-time performance.

articleTitle: An Energy Bus-Based Automatic Modeling Method and Its Application on Joint Planning of Energy Station Capacity and Inside Topology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel energy bus-based automatic modeling method, which has the advantages of high extensibility and practicality. The proposed modeling method is applied to the energy station planning, which can optimize the capacity and inside topology simultaneously without any presupposition of the inside structure. Firstly, the traditional energy bus model is modified by introducing the distribution bus and defining the rules of energy flow. The concept of the digraph is utilized to model the energy station automatically, in which energy converters and connections are abstracted as nodes and edges. Then, the joint planning model considering the maintenance cost of the hardware-based real connections is constructed. Constraints mainly include energy conversion, power balance, inside topology, and the overall energy efficiency ratio (EER). The model is transformed into a mixed-integer linear program by the big M method and solved by Gurobi. Case studies based on a modified integrated energy system illustrate the validity of the proposed method. Results indicate the profound influences of the maintenance cost of real connections, energy price, and the overall EER limit on energy station planning.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Generation Expansion Planning Considering Large-scale Displacement of Fossil Fuel-Fired Units
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the large-scale displacement of fossil fuel-tired units due to the increasing penetration of renewable generation, the generation expansion planning (GEP) problem has been facing a major challenge to deal with the renewable power uncertainty. To handle this issue, this paper introduces a distributionally robust GEP model which explicitly considering the large-scale displacement of fossil fuel-fired units. In the first stage, the long-period generation expansion planning takes into account the expectation of the worst case; While, in the second stage, the short-term operation is modeled based on the distributionally robust optimization (DRO). The wind power uncertainties are treated as ambiguity sets using the Wasserstein distance technique. Aiming to ease the computational complexity of the proposed model, Benders decomposition with a reformulation technique to deal with the worst-case constraints is introduced. Case studies on a modified IEEE RTS-79 system verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Reliability Value of Distributed PV+Storage against Household Blackout
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Distributed energy resource (DER) has been proven as an effective and promising solution to enhance power system resilience and improve household-level reliability. In this paper, we propose a method for evaluating the reliability value of photovoltaic (PV) + battery storage system (BSS) when considering the probability of grid outages leading to household blackouts. Considering such reliability value, economic profit and capital cost of PV+BSS, a simple formula is derived to calculate the optimal planning strategy. This strategy can provide household-level customers with a simple and straightforward expression of invested PV+BSS capacity. Based on 600 households in 8 zones of the U.S. from 2006 to 2015, case studies demonstrate that by adding reliability value on top of economic profit, households can invest in larger PV+BSS to avoid loss of load caused by blackouts. Due to the difference in blackout hours, the households from 8 zones show distinct willingness to install PV+BSS. In the northwest, for example, PV+BSS can offer households with the maximum annual reliability value and total revenue up to $ 251.13 and $ 115.48, respectively.

articleTitle: Three-Stage Three-Phase Interval State Estimation for AC-DC Hybrid Active Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The measurement quality of each node in the active distribution network is quite different and the quantitative interval of the pseudo measurement can be given. The meter accuracy for the real-time measurement can also be expressed by the error interval, so the interval state estimation is an important available choice. Bad data identification is a necessary step to improve the accuracy of state estimation. Because bad data identification for interval state estimation is a mixed integer nonlinear programming problem for which is sensitive to initial value, three-stage interval state estimation is used. In the first stage, linearized model is used to solve the bad data identification problem to provide a better initial value. In the second stage, more accurate bad data identification nonlinear model is used. In the last stage, interval state estimation is performed to estimate intervals of all the variables. In the process of three-phase interval state estimation, the detailed AC-DC hybrid model and distributed generators model are considered.

articleTitle: Fault Location Method for Small Current Grounding System Based on Transient Information
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The transient quantity contains a wealth of fault information after a single-phase ground fault occurs in a small current grounding system. This paper analyzes the transient process after the fault and get the conclusions that the magnitude of the main resonant frequency and its corresponding component is related to the fault distance. The wavelet transform is used to extract the transient information in the main resonant frequency, then the double-end wavelet energy ratio at the scale corresponding to the main resonant frequency is selected as the positioning criterion. Based on this, a fault location method based on the double-ended wavelet energy ratio and back propagation neural network (BPNN) is proposed. The method is based on the spectrum information after the fault, is not affected by the fluctuation of the network load, has distinct advantages in the hybrid line and the branch line, can adapt to the complex network structure of the distribution network. The simulation model with multiple lines is built in PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results show that the proposed method can achieve precise positioning in a single overhead line, cable line, mixed line, and branch line.

articleTitle: A Coordinative optimization and Control Strategy of High Permeability Distributed PV Generation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In recent years, with the depletion of traditional fossil energy, renewable energy such as solar energy and wind energy has been widely used. The development of distributed photovoltaic (PV) is particularly rapid, but the increasing penetration of PV has a significant impact on the security, stability and economy of the distribution network, so it is urgent to research the management of distributed PV and the coordinated control method of joint operation of distribution network. First, taking the community electricity cost and PV consumption of multi-user as the optimization goal, the optimization model of 220V low-voltage distributed PV users is established. Then, the normal boundary intersection (NBI) is used to solve the optimization model, and the technique of order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (TOPSIS) is used to sort and select the compromise solution. At last, the simulation results of different operating conditions are compared, which proves that the demand side resource sharing mechanism has certain economy and further improves the PV capacity.

articleTitle: Smart Metering Planning for Wind Power Accommodation in Multi-energy System Considering Correlated Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This study proposes a new multi-energy system (MES) planning framework for enabling CHP-based energy systems to accommodate growing penetration of renewable energy sources (RES), by utilizing demand response (DR) solutions. Introducing such price-based DR into the multi-energy system entails the investment of smart metering(SM), which results in the concerned problem to be a two-stage optimization program from planning stage to operation stage–-the placement of SM and the pricing strategy for the demand-side are jointly optimized with the RES installation planning to minimize the total economic costs of the system. The proposed two-stage model is developed through a scenario-based stochastic formulation, to explicitly capture the correlated uncertainties from customers’ varying responsivity, energy demand, and the RES generation. The proposed methodology is tested on a modified RES system and the obtained results confirm its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Spinning Reserve Optimization Under Multiple Time Resolution Unit Commitment Module
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Spinning reserve is the unused capacity of synchronized units and it is used to address the unforeseen events during power system operations. This paper proposes a spinning reserve optimization method under the multiple time resolution unified unit commitment and economic dispatch model. Finer time resolution and detailed modeling will be used during the first few hours of the scheduling cycle, while coarser time resolution and simplified modeling will be used during the remaining hours. The spinning reserve is determined by minimizing the running cost, start-up cost, shut-down cost, reserve cost and the expected interruption cost. In order to overcome the computation intractability introduced by EENS, EENS is formulated as linear function of the system spinning reserve. It is found that the multiple time resolution model is fit for determining multiple type of reserves rather than single type of reserve. The efficiency and validity of the proposed method is verified using the IEEE-RTS system.

articleTitle: Reactive Power optimization of Distribution Network with Large-scale Underground Cables Considering Power Factor Constraints
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: At present, capacitive reactive power surplus is becoming increasingly prominent at light load operation in large urban power grid, which hazards the safety and stability of grid. Based on this background, the reactive power optimization method of distribution network with large-scale underground cables is studied. Firstly, an integrated reactive power optimization model with reactor and capacitor is established, taken into consideration power factor constraints. The objective function of the model is to minimize the real power loss. The new constraints include power factor constraints of buses and size constraints of reactors. Then, an improved genetic algorithm is proposed to solve the model. The real power loss sensitivity with respect to reactive power compensation is applied to improve the mutation process. By coordinating the operating and values of capacitors and reactors, the optimized scheme can avoid reactive power reversal and power factor exceeding the limit in the distribution network with large-scale cables access. Finally, a typical high voltage distribution network is used as an example to verify the effectiveness of the model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Sequence Impedance Model and Stability Analysis of MMC Considering Wind Farm Integration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: When the wind power delivery system based on modular multilevel converter (MMC) is connected to the wind farm, interconnected system is prone to produce harmonic resonance. Impedance analysis method is an effective way to analyze the harmonic resonance. This paper develops the ac side impedance of wind farm and wind farm MMC by multiharmonic linearization. The ac side impedance of wind farm MMC considers all control loops and the dc side impedance of grid side MMC. Compared to the existing models, this model can improve the accuracy of the ac side impedance of wind farm MMC and make it easier to analyze the harmonic resonance of the interconnected system. The model can be used for the stability design of MMC-HVDC system connected to wind farm, and the time-domain simulations in Matlab/Simulink validate the impedance model and stability analysis.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Involved in Eliminating Intermittent Two-Stage Robust Optimal Dispatching
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: As renewable energy increasingly connecting into the power grids, the regulation capacity of automatic power generation control (AGC) is gradually decreasing, which is urgent to cooperate with active equipment such as energy storage. In current, dispatch decision-making methods often ignore the intermittent effects of renewable energy. Energy storage can take advantage of its fast regulation rate to better cope with the intermittency of renewable energy based on AGC unit dispatching. Therefore, this paper proposes a two-stage robust optimization dispatching model in which energy storage participates in eliminating intermittency of renewable energy, and abstracts the track of energy storage and AGC units in control as a process between any two moments. This model can make full use of the rapid adjustment capability of energy storage and makes up for the lack of response speed of the AGC unit, improves its climbing ability to release the unit’s adjustment potential, and responds to the intermittent problems of renewable energy power generation. The model is solved by column and constraint generation algorithm (C & CG). The example shows that the model is more robust than the model that does not consider energy storage participates in eliminating intermittent effect and has obvious advantages in economy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Energy Supply Reliability of a New Generation Cyber Physical Energy System Considering Multivariate Information Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In the context of the continuous deepening of energy Internet construction, the coupling degree between information systems and energy supply systems is deepening. In view of the problems that the energy supply reliability of the energy system does not take into account the fault of the information system, and the influence of the fault of the information component on the reliability of the system is not quantitatively analyzed. This paper proposed a cyber physical energy system reliability impact analysis method considering multivariate information disturbance. Firstly, the cyber physical energy system was taken as the research object, and the typical architecture of the cyber physical energy system was introduced. Secondly, the state model of the key equipment in the cyber physical energy system and the static connection and dynamic transmission model of the system were constructed. Besides, the operational characteristics and reliability evaluation indicators were put forward. Finally, the effectiveness and practicability of the proposed evaluation methods were verified by constructing practical cases, and the factors that affecting reliability were further analyzed.

articleTitle: Scheduling Model for Inter-regional HVDC Tie-line Generation and Transmission System Considering Conditional Sections
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The HVDC transmission schedule for clean energy seldom considers the demand of receiving grid. With the expansion of clean energy scale, it brings great pressure to the receiving grid for safe and stable operation. For this reason, a generation and transmission scheduling model of inter-regional HVDC tie-line system considering conditional section is proposed. A step power adjustment model for the HVDC tie-line operation optimization is developed with consideration given to various constraints on tie-line power, which not only give full play to the characteristics of HVDC tie-line that can be flexibly adjusted, but also avoid the frequent conversion of HVDC converter equipment, making the HVDC tie-line schedule more executable. The joint operation model of cascaded hydropower plants in sending grid is established to meet the operational constraints such as the restricted operating zones of hydropower units, and to ensure the priority of clean hydropower resources and the practicability of the hydropower schedule. The model of conditional control section is established, which can effectively deal with the problem of the coupling between the power limits of section and the number of running units, so as to ensure the safe and stable operation of related sections. Based on the actual data of a cross-regional interconnected power grid, the validity of the model is verified, which can promote the accommodation of clean energy across a wide range of regions, reduce the supply cost of large power system, and alleviate the pressure of safe and stable operation at the receiving system.

articleTitle: Research Ideas for the Capacity Configuration of CCHP System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Cooling, heating and power (CCHP) system, which use the generated high-grade thermal energy for generation and the low-grade thermal energy to meet the heating and cooling demand, are research hotspots. Thus the CCHP system can realize a cascade utilization of energy and reduce the emissions. CCHP system can provide the users with the cooling, heating and power demands; therefore it is a high coupling system with multiple equipment and complicated structure, which poses a challenge for the optimal configuration and the performance evaluation of system. We analysis the configuration under “fixing power based on heat” and “fixing heat based on power” mode. Numerical results show that system's comprehensive energy utilization rate reaches best when the model of gas turbine matches the model of absorption refrigerator. In this operating mode, the annual total cost is lower than the other time. Moreover, generally speaking, the economic performance of "fixing heat based on power" operating mode is better than "fixing power based on heat" operating mode.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimal Operating Time of Family Transferable Load
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the continuous development of social economy and technology, social demand for electricity increases year by year.Facing increasingly severe shortage of energy demand, it is an effective way to solve the energy shortage by reasonably and effectively increasing the energy utilization rate of the household electricity load.This paper studies the optimization strategy about operating time of family transferable load.Meanwhile, a programming model of transferable load and the evaluation index of the influence degree of electricity comfort are established.This index can accurately reflect the impact of the change in the operating time of the transferable load on the user's electricity comfort.Besides,the operation mechanism of the genetic algorithm is introduced in detail, and the genetic algorithm is used to optimize the operating time of the transferable load under the premise of ensuring a certain degree of influence on the user's electricity comfort.Finally, an example of 11 tasks with six transferable loads is established, and the strategy is simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Active Power Flow Analysis Based on Nash Equilibrium Method of Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Since electric power is considered a kind of commodity, power flow distribution should be a certain reflection of economic relationships between power generation and demand of energy markets. However, this point of view is not sufficiently explained in conventional power flow analysis. Thus, a game model is established in this study based on basic relations of power transmission to substantially reveal the internal economic characteristic of active power flow. Then, an algorithm is proposed to solve the game model by evolutionary computation. The results of the algorithm illustrate that the Nash equilibrium is satisfied in the active power balance between sending and receiving buses. According to the test studies, the game model driven by economic activations generates conform active power distribution results compared to the results obtained by the Newton method. Consequently, it is demonstrated that the Nash equilibrium exists in the active power flow. This study proposes a method to reveal steady features and compositions of power flow by tracing power flow distribution in terms of a gradual dynamic process.

articleTitle: Influence of regional climate characteristics on short-term photovoltaic power prediction based on fuzzy c-means clustering and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: As a kind of energy from the sun, solar energy is recognized as one of the most competitive renewable energy sources due to its inexhaustible and pollution-free nature. IN recent years, photovoltaic grid capacity is gradually increasing. However, the output of photovoltaic power station is affected by various meteorological factors to different degrees, which makes the output of photovoltaic power station show obvious periodicity and uncertainty. Therefore, photovoltaic power prediction is of great significance for the safety and economic operation of photovoltaic power stations. In order to improve the accuracy of the prediction, a climate impact model suitable for the power prediction of photovoltaic power stations was established for short-term power prediction objects. In this paper, strong meteorological factors are selected as input factors of fuzzy c-means clustering (FCM) algorithm. The original photovoltaic output data were clustered according to the weather type, and they were grouped into three differed<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sub> not weather categories: sunny day, cloudy day and rainy day. The influence of different weather conditions on photovoltaic prediction was analyzed based on the algorithm of convolutional neural network to study the effects of different climates on predictions. It provides the data basis for the establishment of short-term prediction model of photovoltaic output.

articleTitle: Stochastic Day-Ahead Scheduling of ElectricityGas Coupled Systems via Progressive Hedging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the intensification of synergy between different energy systems, coupling between power and natural gas systems has been laboriously investigated. Here we apply Progressive Hedging, a scenario-based decomposition method, for efficient stochastic day-ahead scheduling in the dynamic electricity-gas coupled system. Combined with the iteration-free second-order cone relaxation method, a total of merely $\sim 60$ s is required to complete a 15-scenario stochastic optimization, in a medium-scale coupled network. Also, thanks to the algorithm’s support for parallel computing, the computation time can be further reduced to $\sim$35s with 4 workers running in parallel. Results yielded via Progressive Hedging have been compared with those via traditional stochastic programming and via Benders Decomposition. High accuracy in unit commitment and expected cost is proved to be restored after the introduction of this heuristic algorithm.

articleTitle: The Impact Factors Modeling of WPREs in Electric Power System Based on Orthogonal Test Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In an electric power system with a high penetration of wind power, wind power ramps events (WPREs) has been an important factor of wind power integration and development. To predict them accurately and adopt a timely response, it is important to understand their characteristics. Wind power ramps are affected by various factors and in a complicated way that differ in different wind farms. To give insight into wind power ramps and their dependencies, an impact factors model of wind power ramps has been developed based on orthogonal test theory. By classifying the possible impact factors of wind power ramps into several grade levels and comparing the difference of orthogonal test results brought by each factor, the model enables: compare the effect strength of factors quantitatively; and determine the dominant factors, as well as grade level combinations of these factors with the highest risk of wind power ramps. A wind farm from China is used to illustrate the analysis and verify its feasibility. The main advantage of this model is shown to be: (1) The model can be generalized to any wind farm to explore the factors affecting the wind power ramps; (2) Not only the impact of factors themselves but also the interaction among the factors can be assessed; (3) Any parameter of wind power ramps could be analyzed as experimental index, realizing the analysis of wind power ramps from various aspects.

articleTitle: Study on Heating Capability of Electric and Heating Integrated Energy System in the Background of Flexibility Transformation of CHP Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In order to solve the issue of "wind-heat conflict" during the heating period in north China, this paper proposed a feasibility plan for increasing the heating capability of CHP unit, and established a heating potential model for CHP unit. Then, this paper established the heating capability model to maximize the heating capability of the system when renewable energy is preferentially integrated. Based on the actual structure and data of power sources in a provincial power grid in north China, this paper analyzed the effectiveness of low-pressure cylinder cut-off and electric boiler to enhance the heating capability of electric and heating integrated energy system. The heating capability of the provincial electric and heating integrated energy system can be obtained considering the priority consumption for renewable energy. The proposed method and related conclusions can provide a reference for the development of heating planning.

articleTitle: Distributionally Multi-level Co-optimization Dispatch Considering Primary and Secondary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Distributed energy resource (DER) including wind power, solar energy and energy storage system (ESS) are connected to the active distribution network (ADN) in various combination ways, which makes the distribution network have interaction. As a bridge connecting the transmission grid (TG) and micro grid (MG), ADN breaks the traditional operation pattern of TG+ADN+MG. Considering the physical connections and shared information among TG, ADN and MG, this paper proposes a decentralized and parallel analytical target cascading (ATC) algorithm for TG+ADN+MG multi-level co-optimization dispatch considering primary and secondary frequency regulation. To explore the synergistic ability of the TG+ADN+MG coping with uncertainties of DER, i.e., wind power, the primary and secondary frequency regulation of TG are implemented to cope with uncertainties. Furthermore, the distributional uncertainties of wind power and load are well modeled by data driven, which is proposed in our previous work [1]. An improved 6-bus system is used to test the proposed model, the numerical results illustrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Reserve optimization Model in the Integrated Energy System Considering the Uncertainty of Wind Power and Photovoltaic
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The rapid development of the integration of renewable energy has led to a requirement of the efficient and cutting-edge integrated energy system. Due to the uncertainty of the generation of wind power and photovoltaic, an effective reserve method can be used to maintain the reliability of the power system. The traditional model cannot take the operation mode of new kinds of generators such as CCGTs into consideration, which results in the over-optimistic reserve allocation under reserve market conditions. Therefore, a reserve allocation model considering the uncertainty of the wind power and photovoltaic in the integrated energy system was established in this paper. In this integrated energy system, combined-cycle gas turbine was used as the electricity-gas coupling form. The case study shows that this reserve optimization model can work effectively and overcome the overestimate problem of the ramping ability of the combined-cycle gas machine and the shortage problem of the actual shortage.

articleTitle: Valve Power Loss Fast Evaluation Method for Modular Multi-level Converter Operating at High-Frequency
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The standard IEC 62751 proposed a valve power loss evaluation method combing analytical formulae and numerical simulation for modular multilevel converter (MMC). However, the illustration of building a MMC model and processing simulation results have not been addressed. And also, obtaining solutions from a diodes and IGBTs based simulation model can cost excessively long time. A fast power loss evaluation method is proposed in this paper by linking the PSCAD/EMTDC and Matlab files. Detailed valve power loss analysis of a 201-level 500MW MMC operating at 50Hz~1000Hz is then presented. Relationship between the valve power loss, power transfer level and operating frequencies are presented and fitted. Research results of this paper can be used as guidance for the application of medium and high frequency MMC.

articleTitle: Decentralized Programming of Energy Storage System for the Promotion of Wind Power Consumption in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The environmental pollution and ecological damage caused by conventional energy source result in a great demand of renewable energy including wind power and photovoltaic. Especially in modern power system, wind farms have been wildly constructed and deployed. However, along with the increasing penetration of wind power, the operations of power system are significantly influenced due to the fluctuation and uncertainty of wind power. Due to its flexible charging and discharging characteristics, energy storage system (ESS) is considered as an effective tool to deal with the disadvantage of wind power and enhance the controllability of the power grid. In order to Figure out the optimal location and capacity of ESS, this paper presents a two-stage robust optimization model which takes the fluctuation and uncertainty of wind power into account. Additionally to find out the optimized solution, the second-order cone relaxation technique is adopted to guarantee the global optimal solution. Moreover, the strong duality theorem is employed to convert the optimal operation problem with max-min structure into an equivalent maximization problem. Finally, the model is solved by column and constraint generation algorithm. Experiment results indicate the effectiveness of the presented method in dealing with the ESS optimal allocation issues by considering the uncertainty of wind power.

articleTitle: Combined Probabilistic Prediction of Distributed Wind Power Based on WRF
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: At present, with the increase in the proportion of distributed wind power, the difficulty of its acceptance by the power grid has gradually increased, and the problem of wind abandonment has become prominent. Therefore, accurate prediction of distributed wind power is necessary. However, most of the current wind power forecasting technologies are aimed at centralized wind farms. Considering the characteristics of distributed wind power, this paper proposes a distributed wind power forecasting method based on WRF. This method obtains historical numerical weather prediction (NWP) data of distributed wind farms through WRF model back calculation, then analyzes the cross-correlation of NWP data and historical wind power and the autocorrelation of historical wind power to select the appropriate explanatory variables, and then trains the combined model of sparse Bayesian learning (SBL), kernel density estimation (KDE), and beta distribution estimation (BDE). Case study confirms the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Modeling of Photovoltaic Grid-connected Inverter and Low Voltage Ride-Through Control
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Low voltage ride through (LVRT) requires distributed photovoltaic power generation to continue grid-connected operation in the event of a grid drop, and to provide active or reactive power support for the grid, which can help the grid voltage and grid frequency to remain stable. Aiming at the high-precision test of the control system of grid-connected photovoltaic inverter with LCL filter, especially in the simulation environment from real-time historical data of irradiation, weather and grid condition, this paper proposes a cyber-physical system (CPS) based on hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) method for LVRT test. This paper firstly analyzes the requirements of LVRT, gives the selection range of LCL filter parameters, the design of phase-locked loop design, and the control strategies of low voltage ride through. Then it establishes and simulates the grid-connected inverter model and uses a HIL simulator device to build a CPS control system test platform. Finally, The HIL test results are compared with similar software simulation research results to verify the effect.

articleTitle: Determination of Disturbance Time and Location Based on Synchronous Data
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the increasing activity of industry and commerce in power system, the information extraction and disturbance determination of power grid data are very important to the stable operation of power system. This paper presents a method to identify disturbance time and disturbance location of high and low voltage power grid based on Gaussian KPCA. The Squared Prediction Error (SPE) statistics and Hotelling-T2 statistics (T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> statistics for short) of the measured data are calculated to identify the operation state of the power grid. Then the contribution degree of each variable is calculated, and the disturbance location is determined according to the contribution degree. Finally, the method is applied to three cases, and the result is consistent with the disturbance in cases.

Author Keywords: high and low voltage power grid

articleTitle: Flexible Air Conditioning Loads as Voltage/Frequency-Responsive Sources in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In renewables embedded microgrid system, the intermittent power sources and time-varying load demand can always induce voltage/frequency (v/f) stability issues. It is indispensable to retain sufficient power reserve so as to complement the instant generation-demand imbalance in real time. This paper investigates a novel air conditioning control framework, which is hooked up with a fully controllable PWM converter for re/active power regulation. Based on this new architecture, the air conditioning load (ACLs) is enabled to operate as a v/f responsive source beyond its original energy-consuming functionality. Toward this end, we propose an enhanced air conditioning (EAC) scheme based on model predictive control (MPC), through which the ACLs act as flexible loads to provide frequency reserve and reactive power compensation. Case studies on a small-scale microgrid are carried out, of which simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Risk-Based Robust Multi-Area Dynamic Economic Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage risk-based robust dynamic economic dispatch (RRDED) model for interconnected multi-area power systems. Different from traditional robust optimization, the proposed model applies a flexible uncertainty set rather than a pre-defined one. Based on that, the operational risk is optimized together with the economic dispatch and reserve schedules, with a reasonable admissible region of wind power obtained correspondingly. Besides, the RRDED model schedules not only the base-state tie-line power but also the adjustable range of tie-lines, which enables reserve sharing among areas to handle wind uncertainty. A fully distributed framework based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is presented to solve this model in a decentralized way, with the global optimal solution obtained via finite iterations. Since only limited information needs to be exchanged between the interconnected areas, the communication burden is light and regional information is encrypted. Case studies on a 3-area 354-bus system illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and approach.

articleTitle: A New Coordinated Control Strategy of Flywheel Energy Storage System Participating in Primary Frequency Regulation of Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a new coordinated control strategy for conventional thermal generators with the application of flywheel energy storage system (FESS) to participate in power grid primary frequency regulation (PFR). Through probability density analysis of power grid frequency distribution characteristics, this paper finds that small frequency fluctuation data accounts for more than 80% of total frequency data and proposes that frequency regulation assignments under small disturbances should be undertaken by FESS alone which can significantly reduce generator governor operation times. Comprehensively analyzing power grid frequency regulation requirement and FESS state of charge (SOC) recovery requirement, this paper designs the control rules of FESS output power and then proposes the detailed control strategies in four different working modes. As for frequency regulation indexes, the number of governor operations representing generator wear and tear is included as a new index to help evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. Finally, Matlab/Simulink is used to simulate a typical PFR system with FESS and the simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can effectively improve the frequency quality, maintain a good SOC level, reduce the number of governor operations thereby has good regulation effects.

articleTitle: A Machine-Learning Based Method to Analyze the Correlation between Meteorological Data and Component Outages of Power System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Apart from the operating conditions of power systems, weather conditions have great impact on the reliability performance of the components in power systems. Analyzing the underlying correlation between weather conditions and component outages will be essential to the operating reliability of the systems. This paper proposes a machine-learning based method to analyze the underlying correlation based on real time data. A data enhancement method is also proposed in case the realistic data are insufficient or unavailable. Case studies based on realistic meteorological data of 5 areas in Fujian, China, combined with the IEEE RTS-96 system, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-stage Power Source and Grid Coordination Planning Method Considering Grid Load Uniformity
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In view of the increasing uncertainty of power supply and load, the concept of power source and grid coordination uniformity planning is proposed, and the standard deviation of transmission line load rate is taken as the uniformity evaluation index of power source and grid planning. A multi-stage and multi-objective optimization model of power source and grid expansion planning is established to minimize the comprehensive cost of the whole planning cycle. The improved PSO-GA hybrid algorithm is used to solve the model, which improves the efficiency of solution. The analysis of a simple IEEE garver-6 node system shows that the model and the solution method are effective and feasible, and are suitable for the coordinated planning of the power source and grid under the diversified development of power supply and load.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Configuration for EV Fast Charging Station Considering Characteristics of Charging Load and Wind Power Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Fast charging stations play an essential role in the widespread use of electric vehicles (EV), and they have great impacts on the connected distribution network due to their intermittent power fluctuations. Therefore, combined with rapid adjustment feature of the energy storage system (ESS), this paper proposes a configuration method of ESS for EV fast charging station considering characteristics of charging load and wind power fluctuation. The energy storage configuration can alleviate the impacts of fast charging station on distribution network and improve its operation economy at the same time. First, wind power in distribution network is modeled by scenario method, and charging demand in a station is calculated considering EV characteristics as well as probability of driving. Second, taking the optimized total costs of ESS for EV fast charging station within its life cycle as the objective, the configuration model of the ESS in distribution network is established while such factors as investment, operation, and wind curtailment cost and income of arbitrage are considered. Finally, the model is linearized and solved by GAMS. The feasibility and economic efficiency of the proposed model are verified by an improved IEEE-33 node system.

articleTitle: Business Case for Photovoltiac Power Systems for High Energy Industrial Consumers in South Africa
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The utilization of green technologies has become an important issue in the emerging power sector owing to the global increase in power demand and technological advancement that has resulted in a rapid reduction of renewable energy components’ costs. The use of photovoltaic (PV) as a feasible supplemental energy source to coal-based power plants is investigated in the study. A PV is designed using basic engineering principles and PVGIS tool to determine the validity of the model by using some key economic indicators such as net present value (NPV) of the system, levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) and discounted payback period. The results from the economic analysis show that the system is economically viable for a high industrial energy consumer. The significance of the work shows that the use of PV as a prospective alternative to electricity from the grid is viable. This has reduced the strain on the grid and carbon emission.

articleTitle: Ultra Short-term Output Forecasting of Distributed Photovoltaic Power Station Based on Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: The power output feature of Distributed photovoltaic power stations (DPV) varies dramatically compared to the traditional photovoltaic power station due to various local weather conditions. Thus it is of great importance to analyze the output features to improve the power forecasting performance. In this paper, weather conditions of DPV are studied via statistical approach to obtain the distinguish forecasting models, which are suitable for sunny day, cloudy day, rainy day and foggy day. Then within each model, the clustering algorithm is applied to select most influencing elements among ambient temperature, radiation intensity, local weather, wind speed and direction. Case study shows that the precision of the proposed algorithm is improved by 0.07% (MAPE) and 31MW (RMSE) compared to the traditional neural network forecasting algorithm.

articleTitle: Aggregating Energy Storage in Virtual Power Plant and Its Application in Unit Commitment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: In order to give full play to the positive role of distributed energy storage systems in renewable energy grids, this paper studies the optimization of unit portfolios with virtual power plants. A distributed energy storage flexibility interval aggregation method based on Minkowski Sum and convex edge detection is proposed to aggregate multiple distributed energy storage into a virtual power plant. In this paper, the multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm is adopted to solve the multi-objective optimization problem of optimal output and energy storage charging and discharging successfully by considering the conventional constraints of horizontal parallel units and the energy conservation and capacity constraints of longitudinal energy storage in the same scheduling interval. The results of case studies show that the virtual power plant scheduling scheme optimized by MOPSO has a significant effect on peaking and valley filling, eliminating renewable energy and reducing operating costs.

articleTitle: Power Flow Calculation for Distribution System with Multi-port PETs An Improved AC/DC Decoupling Iterative Method
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: Power electronic transformers (PET) have received widespread attention in recent years due to their flexible networking, diverse operating modes and rich control objects. In this paper, considering the topology, power balance, loss and control characteristics of multi-port PET, we established the steady-state model of PET and applied the proposed steady-state model to the power flow calculation of AC/DC hybrid systems with PET. In order to solve the new problems caused by the introduction of PET port equations and governing equations to power flow calculation, this paper proposes an iterative method of AC/DC mixed power flow decoupling based on step optimization, which can achieve AC/DC decoupling and effectively improve the convergence. At the same time, the proposed algorithm improves the iterative method and overcomes the over-correction and initial value sensitivity problems of the traditional iterative algorithm.

articleTitle: Generation Expansion Planning Restricted by Primary Frequency Response
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE/IAS Industrial and Commercial Power System Asia (I&CPS Asia)
abstract: With the penetration of high proportion of renewable energy resources, the inertia capability of power system becomes the bottleneck to restrict the development of renewable energy. However, the existing research and practice fail to consider the requirement of primary frequency response (PFR) when making the generation expansion plan of renewable energy resources such as wind power. In this paper, we propose an optimal generation expansion planning framework for wind and thermal power plants with PFR restricted.
